diagnostic_evidence.quote: We say a function \mu(y,z,v) is cylindrical on \real^{3d} if for some \tilde \mu\colon \real^{2d}\to \real we have \mu(y,z,v)=\tilde \mu(u,v)$  for all $u=((y\odot y)+(z\odot z))^{1/2}.

issues.failure_explanation: If p(t,·) is the Lebesgue density of (y,z,v)_t and is cylindrical, the Lebesgue density of (u,v)_t is rho(t,(u,v)) = (2 pi)^d (prod_i u_i) p(t,(y,z,v)), since dy_i dz_i = u_i du_i dtheta_i. As stated, the equality of the two densities is off by the factor (2 pi)^d prod_i u_i; this is confirmed by the invariant measures, where the Cartesian density propto exp(-beta(lambda/2)||x_vec||^2 - beta G_3) pushes forward to exactly prod_i u_i times it, matching the prod_i u_i factor in \eqref{pi}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate \eqref{agree} with the factor (2 pi)^d prod_i u_i (or define rho(t,·) as the cylindrical profile consistently).
issues.overall_effect: The displayed identity in Theorem wp is false as an equality of Lebesgue densities. The qualitative transfers in wp (strong Feller, irreducibility) and the entropy decay in thm_bndd_G survive, because H(p(t)|pi_3) = H(rho(t)|pi) holds once the factor is included.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The function $G_{3}$ is locally bounded under \cref{reg1}, and solutions of \cref{cyl} are well defined.
$G_{3}(\vec x)= G( (y\odot y + z\odot z)^{1/2} \odot v)$

issues.failure_explanation: The drift of \eqref{cyl} is -lambda x_vec - grad G_3(x_vec) with ∂_{y_i}G_3 = [grad G(u⊙v)]_i v_i y_i/u_i (likewise for z_i), which has no limit as u_i = (y_i^2+z_i^2)^{1/2} -> 0 when v_i[grad G]_i != 0 (e.g. G(x)=arctan(x_1), approaching along z_i=0 versus y_i=0). The drift is therefore discontinuous (not locally Lipschitz) on {y_i=z_i=0}; the cited existence/uniqueness and strong Feller/density results are not applied within their standard (locally Lipschitz) hypotheses, and the remark that G_3 is locally bounded does not by itself yield well-definedness or uniqueness. A nontrivial extra argument is required (e.g. strong existence/uniqueness and strong Feller for bounded measurable drift with nondegenerate additive noise, or the paper's own Girsanov route in lem:novikov/prop:added-1).

failure_location.quote: \cite[Theorem 10.2.2]{Stroock2013-df} applies to \cref{cyl} and the solution \vec x_t is well-defined on finite-time intervals. \cite[Corollary 10.1.4]{Stroock2013-df} gives that \vec x_t is strong Feller and has a well-defined probability density function.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a contained argument: strong existence/uniqueness for \eqref{cyl} with bounded measurable drift and additive nondegenerate noise (Veretennikov-type), with strong Feller/density via Girsanov; or bypass \eqref{cyl} by constructing \eqref{main} from the CIR/OU reference via the Girsanov transformation of lem:novikov plus pathwise uniqueness up to the (never attained) boundary, obtaining strong Feller from prop:added-1.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem wp's conclusions (existence and uniqueness, positivity, moment bounds, strong Feller, irreducibility, density transfer) are not justified as written, and every ergodicity and convergence result built on wp inherits the gap.
issues.title: Well-posedness, strong Feller and density of \eqref{cyl} invoked for a discontinuous drift
issues.why_classification: All conclusions are correct and recoverable by standard but nontrivial arguments already close to the paper's own tools (its second, Girsanov-based approach), so there is no major loss; but the repair is a genuine supplementary argument about a discontinuous drift, not a routine citation or condition tweak.

issues.failure_explanation: The singular drift (1/beta) int_s^t u_{i,r}^{-1}dr is controlled only via the inverse-moment bounds of cor, which hold for orders strictly below 2; Holder's inequality then yields E||(u,v)_t-(u,v)_s||^q <= c |t-s|^{q(1/2-epsilon)}, exactly as the proof's own final line states. The epsilon-free exponent q/2 claimed in part 1 is not established, and for q >= 2 no argument in the paper can give it (inverse moments of order >= 2 are infinite and the int u^{-1} drift is expected to contribute at least a logarithmic correction).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate part 1 with exponent q(1/2-epsilon) (constant depending on epsilon, q, T), matching what is proved.
issues.overall_effect: Part 1 of timeregbnd overstates the proved regularity. Downstream uses (part 2 of timeregbnd and prop:error_under_bounded_ball) only require the epsilon-dependent version, and the final strong-convergence rate already carries a Delta t^{1/2-epsilon} loss, so no other result changes.

issues.why_classification: A limited weakening of an auxiliary estimate that leaves every downstream statement and the advertised Delta t^{1/2-epsilon} rate intact; no new argument is needed beyond what the proof already contains.

issues.failure_explanation: The true Ito drift correction is the Euclidean row-divergence nabla·M = (3/2, x/(2 eta))^T — the same vector appearing in the proof's own Fokker-Planck expansion. Under the paper's convention div_g(V) = |g|^{-1/2} sum_j ∂_j(V_j |g|^{1/2}) with |M| = prod_i 4 eta_i^2, one instead computes div_{M^{-1}}(M) = (1/2, 0)^T, which equals neither nabla·M nor the claimed (1/2)binom(1, x/eta). The identity mu = -M grad H + (1/2)binom(1, x/eta) already fails in the eta-component: mu_eta contains +1 (Ito correction of u_i^2/4) while -M grad H + 1/2 contributes -1/2 + 1/2 = 0. Hence the SDE as stated does not generate the (correct) Fokker-Planck equation proved below it.

issues.why_classification: The repair is a local correction of the drift-correction term; the proposition's verified content (the Fokker-Planck equation and the mirror metric) and the advertised link survive unchanged, and the result has no dependents.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: standard theory (Bakry--Emery criterion, Holley--Stroock theorem) applies to the potential $\frac 12 \lambda \|\vec x \|^2+G_3(\vec x)$, as it is a bounded perturbation (given by $G$) of a convex potential (given by $\frac12\lambda\|\vec x\|^2$).

issues.failure_explanation: The invariant density is proportional to exp(-beta( (lambda/2)||x_vec||^2 + G_3 )), so the bounded perturbation of the log-density is beta G_3, with oscillation beta(sup G - inf G). Bakry-Emery (LSI constant beta lambda for the Gaussian part) combined with Holley-Stroock therefore gives R = beta lambda e^{-beta(sup G - inf G)}, not beta lambda e^{inf G - sup G}. The explicit rate in \eqref{hhh} is wrong whenever beta != 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace R by beta lambda e^{beta(inf G - sup G)}.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised exponential rate in thm_bndd_G is quantitatively wrong (too large when beta(sup G - inf G) > 0); the qualitative conclusion of geometric convergence in relative entropy is unaffected.
issues.title: Holley-Stroock factor in the LSI rate misses a factor beta
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol, forced correction of an explicit constant; the theorem's qualitative content (geometric entropy decay) and all other results are unchanged.

Theorem num_erg assumes only reg1, i.e. arbitrary Delta t > 0, so for Delta t >= lambda/B^2 the proof's Lyapunov condition is not available (and the displayed bound can fail); the omitted hypothesis is needed by the argument.

\log(P)(x, \hat x) &= -\frac{\beta}{4\tstep} \norm{   (1+\tstep\,\lambda) u^{k+1} - \frac{\tstep}{\beta u^{k+1}} - u^k  + \tstep\, v^k\odot \nabla G(u^k\odot v^k) ) }^2

issues.failure_explanation: The finite-time error step invokes thm:num_conv with initial law tilde pi_Delta-t, which must satisfy reg3(ii), i.e. d(tilde pi_Delta-t)/d pi uniformly bounded. Truncation to a ball does not ensure this: pi vanishes like prod_i u_i at the boundary {u_i=0} inside B_R, while the chain's invariant density near u_i = 0 is governed by a kernel behaving like exp(-Delta t/(4 beta u_i^2) - w_i/(2 u_i)) mixed against pi_Delta-t, which is not shown to be controlled by pi. Hence tilde pi_Delta-t need not have a bounded ratio to pi, and the reduction to reg3 is unjustified as written.

failure_location.quote: If $\pi_\tstep$ does not satisfy \cref{reg3}, we may replace $\pi_\tstep$ with  a regularised distribution $\tilde \pi_\tstep$. For example, let $\tilde{\pi}_\tstep(\cdot)=\pi_\tstep(\cdot \cap B_R) /\pi_\tstep(B_R)$ for the ball $B_R$ of radius $R=\tstep^{-1}$).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Regularize the Radon-Nikodym derivative instead, e.g. d(tilde pi_Delta-t) propto min(d pi_Delta-t/d pi, K) d pi (legal since both measures have positive smooth densities on X), which gives a uniformly bounded ratio, total-variation convergence to pi_Delta-t as K -> infty, and inherits the uniform V-moment bound.
issues.overall_effect: The proof's reduction of pi_Delta-t to an initial law satisfying reg3 is not established, so the convergence of pi_Delta-t(phi) to pi(phi) is not fully proved as written; the statement itself remains true under a valid regularization.
issues.title: Ball-truncation regularization of pi_Delta-t does not deliver the bounded density ratio required by reg3
issues.why_classification: A short, routine alternative regularization repairs the step and preserves the theorem's statement and every guarantee; no new global argument or weakening of the claim is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: Three defects share one root. (i) As defined, ||x||_{1,2} = sum_j ||x_{b_j}||^2 = ||x||_2^2, which is not the group-l1 norm sum_j ||x_{b_j}|| (and makes the prior smooth). (ii) The displayed single-eta integral equals e^{-a||x||_2} by \eqref{eq:laplace}, matching neither the stated definition nor the standard group norm. (iii) For a group b_i of size d_i, the change x_{b_i} = u_i v_{b_i}, eta_i = u_i^2/(beta lambda) carries the Jacobian factor u_i^{d_i}, so the induced density is proportional to prod_i u_i^{d_i} exp(-(beta lambda/2)(||u||^2+||v||^2) - beta G(u⊙v)); the stated prod_{i=1}^K u_i is correct only for singleton groups, and with it the x-marginal is a Bessel-K type density, not exp(-beta lambda ||x||_{1,2} - beta G(x)). Consequently the u-drift acquires d_i/(beta u_i) in place of 1/(beta u_i), so the Langevin dynamics are not 'identical to the l1 setting' as claimed.
